This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Taipei Songshan Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 10 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Taipei Songshan Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/tw/taipei/RCSS.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent monsoon conditions over northern India, including widespread cloud cover and scattered thundershowers tracked by the India Meteorological Department, have moderated daytime heating in Lucknow, keeping maximum temperatures near seasonal norms of 31–33 °C. Official forecasts for August 10 consistently project a high of 32–33 °C with patchy rain and humidity above 70 percent, limiting solar insolation and preventing the stronger warming that would push readings to 34 °C or above. Model consensus from multiple sources shows only minor day-to-day variability, with no major heat-wave signals or clear-sky periods emerging in the past 48 hours to alter that range. Trader positioning therefore concentrates on the narrow 32–33 °C band, reflecting both the stabilizing effect of active monsoon flow and the low probability of outlier intensification or suppression before the day’s peak is recorded.

eventMetadata.context_description: A passing cold front accompanied by an upper-level trough has suppressed daytime heating across the Western Cape, driving trader consensus toward a maximum of 15–16 °C in Cape Town on 10 August. Official guidance from the South African Weather Service and BBC forecasts indicates partly cloudy to showery conditions with fresh to strong southerly winds, limiting insolation and advecting cooler maritime air from the South Atlantic. eventMetadata.context_description: PAGASA’s official outlook for Metro Manila on August 11, 2026, forecasts a daily maximum of 31°C with a 30% rain chance, directly supporting the market’s leading 31°C outcome at 44.5% implied probability. The prevailing southwest monsoon continues to deliver moderate to heavy rains across Luzon, increasing cloud cover and limiting daytime solar heating while enhancing evaporative cooling. These conditions align with August climatology, where average highs hover near 31°C but rarely exceed it under active monsoon flow. Recent model runs show limited warming potential through the period, keeping 30–31°C as the most probable range and explaining why probabilities drop sharply above 32°C or below 29°C. Traders are weighting the latest agency guidance heavily ahead of tomorrow’s resolution.

New model runs and updated NWS discussions through the morning of August 11 will likely tighten the distribution as observational data refine the convective evolution.

Recent model runs show limited spread, though ensemble members allow for modest intensification if subsidence strengthens or urban heat-island effects amplify readings at official stations. A broader European heatwave pattern has already produced upper-90s°F (mid-30s°C) readings in the region, supporting the elevated but not extreme probabilities traders assign to 35–36°C while keeping sub-33°C or 37°C+ outcomes at low implied odds. Updated guidance from the next 48-hour model cycle will likely tighten the distribution ahead of resolution.

Lower outcomes remain possible only if stronger convective activity develops, while 34 °C or higher carries lower odds absent further model support for intensified heating. Updated NEA and global model runs over the next 48 hours will be the key near-term catalysts for any shift in these implied probabilities.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest forecast models from agencies like the Polish IMGW and European ensembles point to a sunny day with light northwesterly winds moderating daytime heating in Warsaw, keeping the maximum near the August climatological average of 23–24 °C. Clear skies will enhance solar radiation, while the Baltic-influenced air mass limits advection of warmer continental air, creating the tight clustering between 23 °C and 24 °C outcomes. Recent stabilization after June’s extreme heatwave has reduced model spread, though small shifts in cloud timing or wind speed could still tip the daily high by 1 °C. Traders’ near-even split between these two bins reflects both the narrow uncertainty range typical of short-range temperature forecasts and the precise resolution criteria used by official stations.
